The trend filter is a hard VETO inside OracleNN, so in bear and sideways years the book is EMPTY - exposure 1-9% - and the worst year is therefore bounded near zero by construction. No sizing, gating or money-management lever can change that, because they all act on trades the system chooses to take. trend_soft turns the veto into a dimmer: a down-trend name may be entered at a fraction of normal size. Read the EFFICIENCY as well as the delta - 2021 gained 399pp for 6.7pp of extra drawdown, which is generous, but the thin years are what decide, and a lever that only amplifies the moonshot year is a worse deal than it looks. Kill: drawdown rises faster than return across the typical years, or the effect lives entirely in 2021.

On the champion's 3,329 trades, chain activity (unique addresses, as a deviation from its own trailing trend) stratifies monotonically: weakest quartile +0.107%/trade at 39% win, strongest +0.867% at 47%. The threshold tested first is the statistical convention (-1.0 sd), not a value swept until it looked good.

why: A systematic decile search for LOSING pockets - the only kind worth vetoing, per P27's rule - says the fear index's losing region does not stop at the Extreme Fear line we currently use: deciles 1-3 all lose (-0.016%, -0.022%, -0.112% per trade at 32-37% win, 958 trades between them), and the third reaches F&G 42. The index's OWN next published boundary is 46, where 'Fear' ends and 'Neutral' begins - so widening the veto to that line is still an external threshold rather than one fitted to our trade map, which is the distinction that made the first veto trustworthy. The same search found the on-chain pockets are scattered and non-monotone: noise, consistent with P27's refutation.

why: The operator's founding request, and somehow never measured directly: the book RANKS by conviction - the scarce slots go to the highest scorer - but then funds every accepted trade identically, so a 0.99 and a 0.76 get the same capital once both are in. This sizes each entry by how far it clears the bar (Kelly's rule: stake in proportion to edge), with the multiplier built to average exactly 1.0 across the conviction range: it REDISTRIBUTES capital rather than adding exposure. That is the distinction the whole ledger points at - every lever that added exposure by admitting worse trades has been refuted here, while the one that redistributed by expectancy (the learned money model) is the largest win on file. It also acts ONCE, at entry, which is where P25 says the evidence is freshest.
judge: Control near +0.0407. Success: positive delta with seeds agreeing AND exposure roughly UNCHANGED - that combination is the proof it redistributed rather than inflated. Kill: exposure rises materially (then the tilt is leverage in disguise), or the gentle arm does nothing while only the strong one moves, which would mean we are reading noise in the top decile of conviction.

why: P29 refuted the first version and named the flaw precisely: unbiased over the RANGE is not unbiased over the POPULATION. Accepted entries cluster just above the bar, so a tilt centred on the midpoint of (enter..1.0) shrank nearly every trade - exposure fell 7.88% to 5.69% and the arms lost in dose order. It was an exposure cut wearing a redistribution's clothes, and cutting exposure has lost every time in this project. The centre is now learned causally from the book's own history - a rolling median of the convictions it has actually accepted, untilted until the window fills - so there is no fitted constant and no lookahead. This is the same idea tested properly, not a new one.
judge: Control near +0.0407. The FIRST thing to read is exposure: if it drifts down again the centring did not work and the result says nothing about sizing by certainty. Only with exposure flat does the delta mean anything. Success: positive delta, seeds agreeing, exposure within a few tenths of baseline. Kill: exposure moves either way, or the effect is monotone in strength with no plateau - a tilt that keeps helping as it grows is usually measuring something else.

why: The labelling threshold decides what counts as a swing worth catching, and it is the one generation knob never tested PAIRED - the champion's 3% came out of the autoloop's search, where band, risk and recipe all moved at once. Everything downstream inherits it: the labels, therefore the net's idea of an opportunity, therefore the trades. With filters, features, labels-by-path, committees and breadth all refuted, the definition of the target itself is the last untested piece of the generation stack that costs only GPU hours.
judge: Baseline must reproduce ~0.138/0.148 under the current shipping config. Success: a variant beats baseline on BOTH seeds - a threshold change alters the whole training target, so a one-seed win is meaningless here. Watch trade counts: a coarser threshold should trade less and hold longer, and if 5% simply trades less and scores the same, the honest reading is that the label scale does not matter, not that coarser is better.
